*[Bug 19132] New: parseNamespaceFile is inconsistent when parsing the importFrom directive*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19132>

            Bug ID: 19132
           Summary: parseNamespaceFile is inconsistent when parsing the
                    importFrom directive
           Product: R
           Version: R 4.6.x
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Linux
            Status: UNCONFIRMED
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Misc
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:tim.taylor@hiddenelephants.co.uk|tim.taylor@hiddenelephants.co.uk>

When parseDirective (internal to parseNamespaceFile) parses

```
importFrom(data.table, .N, `:=`)
```

it returns something akin to

```
[[1]]
[[1]][[1]]
[1] "data.table"

[[1]][[2]]
[1] ".N"   "`:=`"
```

in contrast, when it parses 

```
importFrom(data.table, `:=`)
```

we will get (note the lack of backticks)

```
[[2]]
[[2]][[1]]
[1] "data.table"

[[2]][[2]]
[1] ":="
```

The result is that the first example will not work in a NAMESPACE file (it
needs changing to `importFrom(data.table, .N, ":=")`).

Digging in to the code I believe a solution may be changing [line 1397 in
namespace.R](<https://svn.r-project.org/browse/R/trunk/src/library/base/R/namespace.R?op=blame&rev=89563#l1397>)
from

```
structure(asChar(ivars), names = inames)
```

to

```
structure(vapply(ivars, asChar, ""), names = inames)
```

I've not yet tried a patch as wanted to flag for thoughts.

*[Bug 19133] New: A new matrix method for aperm*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19133>

            Bug ID: 19133
           Summary: A new matrix method for aperm
           Product: R
           Version: R 4.6.x
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Linux
            Status: UNCONFIRMED
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:hugo.gruson+Rbugzilla@normalesup.org|hugo.gruson+Rbugzilla@normalesup.org>

This request is somewhat in the same line as
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19069> in that it offers a
short-circuit for a particular case of `aperm()`.

`?aperm` documentation reads:

> The function t provides a faster and more convenient way of transposing matrices.

Since `aperm()` is a generic function, would it be possible to provide an
`aperm()` method for matrices which would:

- call `t()` if `perm` is `c(1, 2)`
- call the identity otherwise

While I understand the short-circuit is documented in `?aperm`:

- many users will glance over it when reading the documentation
- I am developing a package which needs to permute arrays with an arbitrary
number of dimensions. Currently, if I want to leverage the short-circuit, I
need to "manually dispatch" to `t()` or `aperm()` depending on the number of
dimensions of the array. This is not very elegant, and seems like a waste of a
good opportunity for actual S3 dispatch.

You can see a similar pattern in at least a couple of CRAN or Bioconductor
packages in the wild:

<https://github.com/Huber-group-EMBL/Rarr/blob/697fc75ea74ed5fdd2162d1e20e51eeeaf87a684/R/codecs_array_array.R#L22-L30>

<https://github.com/mlverse/torch/blob/e4de110c1df9130acb9ec927cb220720d9957259/R/tensor.R#L439-L445>

*[Bug 19134] New: iconv() leaks conversion descriptors and a string buffer on some errors*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19134>

            Bug ID: 19134
           Summary: iconv() leaks conversion descriptors and a string
                    buffer on some errors
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Linux
            Status: UNCONFIRMED
          Severity: minor
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:troy@cornball.ai|troy@cornball.ai>

Created attachment 3781
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3781&action=edit>
iconv() leak patch

## Summary

`do_iconv()` allocates a local `R_StringBuffer` and lazily opens conversion
descriptors, but releases them only on normal return. Errors inside the
conversion loop longjmp past that cleanup.

The first reproducer below leaks the buffer and a descriptor; the second leaks
the buffer. On R-devel r90391 with glibc 2.39, LeakSanitizer measured 4,115,200
bytes leaked across 100 runs of the first reproducer.

The trigger is an ordinary type error, not memory pressure, so no unusual
conditions are needed to reach it.

## Affected code

`src/main/sysutils.c`, `do_iconv()`:

```
607:    R_StringBuffer cbuff = {NULL, 0, MAXELTSIZE};   /* function local */
683:    R_AllocStringBuffer(0, &cbuff);
691:            error(_("'x' must be a character vector or a list of NULL or
raw vectors"));
755:            arg_obj = Riconv_open(to, from);
768:                error(_("unsupported conversion from '%s' to '%s'"), from,
to);
929:    if (latin1_obj != (iconv_t)-1) Riconv_close(latin1_obj);
930:    if (utf8_obj != (iconv_t)-1) Riconv_close(utf8_obj);
931:    if (arg_obj != (iconv_t)-1) Riconv_close(arg_obj);
932:    R_FreeStringBuffer(&cbuff);
```

Lines 929-932 are the only releases, and no `begincontext`,
`R_ExecWithCleanup` or `R_UnwindProtect` covers them. Line 691 is inside the
conversion loop, so a descriptor opened for one element is lost when a later
element fails.

## Reproducer

```
## leaks the buffer and a descriptor
iconv(list(charToRaw("a"), 42), from = "latin1", to = "UTF-8")

## leaks the buffer
iconv(list(charToRaw("a")), from = "NOSUCHENC", to = "UTF-8")
```

Repeating either grows the process without bound.

## Measurement

R-devel r90391 built with `clang -fsanitize=address`, 100 runs of the first
reproducer:

```
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 4115200 byte(s) leaked in 400 allocation(s).
```

| allocation site | bytes | objects |
|---|---|---|
| `iconv_open` via `Riconv_open`, `do_iconv:755` | 11,200 | 100 |
| gconv step tables, same path | 3,264,000 | 100 |
| gconv cache lookup, same path | 20,800 | 100 |
| `R_AllocStringBuffer`, `do_iconv:683` | 819,200 | 100 |

41,152 bytes per call. The 8,192-byte string buffer is
implementation-independent; the rest is glibc's gconv allocation and will
differ on other C libraries. Full sanitizer log available on request.

## History

r73116 (2017-08-23) added `Riconv_close(obj)` at both error sites. r82791
(2022-09-02) removed them: it replaced the single pre-loop `obj` with three
descriptors opened lazily inside the loop, at which point one
`Riconv_close(obj)` no longer applies, and the closes were dropped rather than
rewritten. The descriptor close was therefore present in R 3.5.0 through 4.2.x
and absent from 4.3.0 onward. The string buffer has leaked since r41899
(2007-06-10) and was not covered by the 2017 fix.

(PR#17328 shares commit r73116 but is a different defect, `Sys.setlocale()`
leaking cached descriptors; that fix is still correct and in place.)

## Suggested fix

Attached. It registers the releases on the context stack, as `writetable()`
does in `src/library/utils/src/io.c`, rather than re-adding `Riconv_close()` at

text:
*[Bug 19131] Stale lazy-load database cache after re-installing a package in the same session*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19131>

--- Comment #2 from Kevin Ushey (<mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>) ---
Created attachment 3782
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3782&action=edit>
Alternate patch (use file id as gate for caching)

A note on the cost of the fetch-time validation, since it puts a stat()
on a path that previously did no filesystem work at all on a cache hit.

The check runs once per lazyLoadDBfetch() call, i.e. once per first use
of each lazy-loaded object (promises are only forced once), once per
object retrieved from a help database, and once per lazy-data load.
Some measured numbers (macOS arm64, APFS; a warm stat() there is about
0.6 microseconds):

- A full R startup performs ~700 fetches, so validation adds ~0.4 ms
  to a ~180 ms startup.
- tools::Rd_db("stats") performs ~650 fetches: again ~0.4 ms, against
  ~200 ms the workload spends reading, decompressing and unserializing
  the blobs. Per fetch, the stat is well under 0.1% of the work the
  fetch already does.

To report the one number that looks alarming rather than hide it: the
validation does become the largest source of stat() calls in an R
startup (~700 of ~850). But the time is what matters, and the time is
negligible on local filesystems; the pattern of validating a cache
with a stat per use is standard practice elsewhere for exactly that
reason.

Other language runtimes do comparable validation. CPython validates
its bytecode cache with a stat of the .py source when a module is
first imported, comparing the mtime and size recorded in the .pyc
header; once imported, a module is never revalidated, just as a forced
promise never re-fetches. The units differ -- Python's unit of code
loading is the module where R's lazy-load unit is the object -- but
per unit loaded Python touches the filesystem more, not less: on my
machine, importing 130 stdlib modules performed 823 stat/open calls
(path probing, cache validation, opens), about five per module, where
this patch performs exactly one attribute lookup per object fetched.
PHP's opcache is the closest match to the situation being fixed here
-- a long-running process serving compiled artifacts whose files can
be replaced underneath it -- and it revalidates scripts by timestamp
on use, enabled by default (rate-limited to once per 2 seconds per
script).
